program_name: Economic Analysis and Policy (official English name used by UNITO: 'Economic analysis and policy'; the microsite title is "Master's Degree Course in Economic Analysis and Policy"; UNITO also describes it as the "inter-university master's degree program with joint title in Economic Analysis and Policy"). It is the UNITO leg of the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master EPOG-JM | Economic POlicies for the Global bifurcation.
level: master (second-cycle degree / laurea magistrale, 2 years, 120 ECTS)
teaching_language: Fully English-taught, but it is CASE 3 in the sense of the field definition: a joint/interuniversity Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EPOG-JM), not a stand-alone UNITO degree. UNITO 'Key information' states "Course held in English" and Apply@UniTo records "Study language: English"; the thesis must be written in English. Students spend only part of the two years in Turin: Semester 1 always at Università degli Studi di Torino, Semester 2 either at UNITO (Path 1) or at the University of the Witwatersrand, Johannesburg (Path 2), Semester 3 in Paris (joint programme of Université de technologie de Compiègne, Sorbonne Université and Conservatoire national des arts et métiers), Semester 4 'to be defined'. Knowledge of French, Italian or German is not mandatory but is taken into account in the selection. Note: the wider EPOG-JM consortium has a Minor (C4) whose first-year courses are largely taught in Portuguese, but that minor is not hosted by UNITO. [uncertain - whether all EPOG-JM majors/minors lead to the UNITO 'Economic Analysis and Policy' LM-56 title or only the two paths listed on the UNITO microsite]
campus: Turin (Torino), Italy - Department of Cultures, Politics and Society (Culture, Politica e Società), associate department Economics and Statistics 'Cognetti De Martiis', School of Law, Political and Economic-Social Sciences. Apply@UniTo records 'Study location: Italy, Turin'. Because of the compulsory Erasmus Mundus mobility, the UNITO microsite lists the 'Teaching seat: Turin, Johannesburg and Paris'.
degree_class: LM-56 - Scienze dell'economia (Economics). Stated as 'Classification of Degree: LM-56' on both the UNITO microsite 'Key information' page and the Apply@UniTo overview. UNITO internal identifiers: en.unito.it UGOV degree id 39574; Apply@UniTo course id 683, a.y. 2026/27 intake id 33. [uncertain - the short UNITO course code in the 'nnnnMnn' format (e.g. 1502M21) could not be read on any reachable page]
admission_type: Formally an OPEN-ACCESS (free admission, no numerus clausus) second-cycle degree at UNITO - it appears in the official list on en.unito.it 'Postgraduate degrees with free admission' as 'Economic analysis and policy (in collaboration with other French Universities)'. In practice admission is by a COMPETITIVE SELECTION CALL run once a year by the EPOG-JM consortium, not by a written entrance exam: (1) curricular/eligibility check by an appointed committee, (2) preselection by the EPOG-JM Consortium committee on the excellence of the academic record, (3) a videoconference interview (UNITO calls it the TAPP - Personal Preparation Assessment Test, a ca. 15-minute interview via Skype/videoconference), (4) a final main list plus reserve list requiring unanimity of the degree-awarding institutions. Weighted selection criteria published by the consortium: academic records 35%, languages 30%, motivation and recommendation letters 20%, educational background/CV 15%. Applications are NOT made through the normal UNITO 'pre-application to courses with free admission' route on MyUniTO but through the EPOG online application platform. A territory quota exists on Apply@UniTo: 20 places for non-European applicants residing abroad. [uncertain - the coexistence of 'free admission' classification with a quota of 20 non-EU places and a competitive consortium selection is not explained on any reachable UNITO page]
application_deadline_eu: A.y. 2026/2027 (cohort 2026-2028): EPOG application platform opened October 2025; APPLICATION DEADLINE 29 JANUARY 2026 at 13:00 Paris time; interviews 4-6 March 2026; selection results end of March 2026. The same single deadline applies to EU and non-EU applicants (EPOG runs one call for all nationalities). Holders of a foreign qualification must in parallel apply on Apply@UniTo within the UNITO postgraduate window for a.y. 2026-2027: 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026 (EUR 60 application fee, up to two programmes). NEXT CYCLE (cohort 2027-2029, i.e. a.y. 2027/2028): platform opens October 2026, deadline 29 January 2027 at 13:00 Paris time, interviews March 2027, results end of March 2027. [uncertain - UNITO also publishes a 'Second application call for free access postgraduate programs reserved to Italians, EU and EU equivalents, non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy: from 25 August to 8 September 2026'; it could not be verified whether EAP/EPOG accepts applicants through that late call, since the EPOG selection is closed by then]
application_deadline_non_eu: Same single EPOG deadline as for EU applicants: 29 January 2026 at 13:00 Paris time for a.y. 2026/2027 (29 January 2027 for a.y. 2027/2028). Additional steps for non-EU citizens residing abroad: (a) application on Apply@UniTo within 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026 (postgraduate window, EUR 60 fee); (b) pre-enrolment (visa) application on the Universitaly platform by 15 July 2026 for a.y. 2026-2027, choosing one programme only and the competent Italian embassy/consulate; (c) selected students must supply certified/legally attested English translations of their study documents and their proof of English by 10 June, and degree certificates by 31 August if they graduate by 31 July. Apply@UniTo quota: 20 places for non-European applicants residing abroad. [uncertain - no separate non-EU deadline is published by the EPOG consortium; the Universitaly date is the general UNITO 2026-2027 deadline, not a programme-specific one]
entry_exam_or_test: No written entrance examination and no TOLC/SAT/GRE-mandatory test. Selection is document-based plus an INTERVIEW: UNITO calls it the TAPP (Test di Accertamento della Preparazione Personale / Personal Preparation Assessment Test), described on the microsite as a 15-minute interview via Skype, justified by the fact that most applicants come from non-European countries; the EPOG consortium describes the same step as an interview by videoconference organised by the Consortium committee for the preselected applicants. Interview period for a.y. 2026/2027: 4-6 March 2026 (the microsite says 'early March 2026'); for a.y. 2027/2028: March 2027. Passing the TAPP produces the authorisation to enrol. A GRE General Test score (at least 150 verbal reasoning, 4 analytical writing, 151 quantitative reasoning) is optionally accepted as proof of English proficiency, but the GRE is not an admission test. [uncertain - the UNITO 'How to apply' page quotes an older GRE scale (450 verbal, 4.1 analytical writing, 650 quantitative), which conflicts with the current 150/4/151 figures on Apply@UniTo and on the EPOG site]
academic_requirements:
1) QUALIFICATION: a first-cycle degree (Bachelor's or equivalent) of at least 180 ECTS - 'a three-year degree or other qualification obtained abroad recognized as suitable according to current regulations, respecting the criteria established in the Teaching Regulations'. A tertiary degree of bachelor/master/PhD level corresponding to at least 180 ECTS is accepted. For UNITO admission of foreign qualifications the general rule applies: first-cycle or integrated university degree obtained after at least 15 years of total schooling (EQF 6 / ISCED 6), with proof of authenticity; a same-cycle or higher-cycle qualification alone (Master's, PhD) is not sufficient - the first-cycle degree must always be submitted.
2) CURRICULAR CREDITS - two figures are published and they differ. UNITO microsite and Apply@UniTo: 'They must also have 18 CFU in economics and 6 in statistics.' EPOG consortium and the UNITO 'How to apply' page: 'a minimum of 24 ECTS (or equivalent) in economics and 6 ECTS in statistics or econometrics'. The EPOG page reconciles them: 24 ECTS in economics + 6 in statistics/econometrics is the standard requirement, while students with at least 18 ECTS in economics and 6 in statistics 'can be considered' for Major A / Minors C1 and C4, and outstanding candidates below those thresholds may be accepted conditionally and asked to take additional courses. Content of the 24 ECTS varies by Major: Major A accepts any basic/advanced economics and management courses; Major B requires microeconomics and macroeconomics (plus international economics for Minor B1); Minor C1 requires basic/advanced economics; Minor C2 requires micro-, macro- and international economics; Minors C3 and C4 have no specific additional subject requirements.
3) GPA THRESHOLD: 'Candidates' academic records should have a minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) for the Bachelor's degree of at least 70% of the maximum scale' (EPOG selection criteria, weighted 35%).
4) NOT-YET-GRADUATED APPLICANTS: candidates who plan to graduate by 31 July may apply and be provisionally accepted; they must file a sworn statement at application stage and supply the degree certificate by 31 August. UNITO adds that requirement verification can be carried out before the three-year degree is obtained, and candidates lacking the credits are invited either to insert courses in the missing SSDs among their free-choice exams or, after graduating, to enrol in single courses ('corsi singoli') to satisfy the admission requirements.
5) QUOTA / PLACES: Apply@UniTo (a.y. 2026/27) - 'This degree program has 20 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad.' No overall number of places or EU-quota is published; the programme is listed by UNITO among the postgraduate degrees with free (unrestricted) admission. No Marco Polo quota is published for this programme.
6) MOTIVATION: 'a clear motivation for the programme' is an explicit admission requirement; applicants should highlight their interest, knowledge and motivation to engage with heterodox approaches of economics. Compulsory physical mobility applies to all enrolled students, scholarship holders or not.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH is required; no Italian certificate is required (the UNITO CLIQ/CISIA Italian B2 rule applies only to non-EU visa applicants enrolling in Italian-taught free-admission undergraduate or single-cycle programmes, so it does not apply here).
LEVELS PUBLISHED ON UNITO PAGES (Apply@UniTo 'Language requirements' and the microsite 'How to apply'): TOEFL computer-based 237 / paper-based 580 / internet-based (iBT) 87 or above; IELTS 6.5 Academic; Cambridge C2 Proficiency (CPE) grade C; Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE) grade B; CEFR B2. A GRE General Test with at least 150 verbal reasoning, 4 analytical writing and 151 quantitative reasoning is also accepted as proof of English (the microsite version of the same sentence quotes the old GRE scale: 450 / 4.1 / 650).
HIGHER LEVELS PUBLISHED BY THE EPOG CONSORTIUM (the body that actually runs the selection, current live page): CEFR C1 or more; TOEFL iBT 95 or more (MyBest Scores accepted); IELTS 7.0 or more (Academic); C1 Advanced (CAE) grade B or more; C2 Proficiency (CPE) grade C or more; PTE Academic 67 or more; or the GRE 150/4/151 alternative.
EXEMPTIONS: no individual test is required for English native speakers or for applicants who hold a higher education degree entirely taught in English; in that case (or if the test result is not available by the submission deadline) a sworn statement on the official EPOG form must be uploaded. Proof of English must be provided no later than 10 JUNE.
OTHER LANGUAGES: knowledge of French, Italian or German is not mandatory but is taken into account in the selection (languages carry 30% of the selection score); those students must provide official proof (foreign language diploma or the DIALANG European test). [uncertain - the UNITO-published minimum (B2 / IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 87) and the EPOG-published minimum (C1 / IELTS 7.0 / TOEFL iBT 95) conflict; the EPOG figures are on a live, more recently updated page and are almost certainly the operative ones, but the UNITO pages had not been aligned at the time of research]
required_documents:
A. EPOG ONLINE APPLICATION (the actual admission file; everything is uploaded in the Attachments section of the online form at application.epog.eu - documents must NOT be sent by email):
1. Completed online application form.
2. Full curriculum vitae (Europass format suggested, not mandatory).
3. Scanned copy of at least one relevant diploma proving a tertiary degree of at least 180 ECTS (bachelor/master/PhD). If not issued in English, an English translation is needed (an unofficial translation is accepted at application stage; an official one is required if pre-selected). Applicants graduating by 31 July upload the official sworn statement form instead, and supply the certificate by 31 August.
4. Scanned copy of all higher-education academic records / transcripts in their original version, including all courses completed at the time of application (not only the current year), with English translation if applicable. Selected students must provide a certified (legally attested) English translation by 10 June at the latest. The transcripts must evidence the minimum ECTS in economics and statistics/econometrics and the Major/Minor-specific requirements. The diploma supplement is encouraged if available.
5. Proof of English language proficiency (by 10 June), or the sworn-statement exemption form for native speakers / holders of an English-taught degree. Non-mandatory proof of French, Italian or German proficiency.
6. Statement of purpose, max 500 words, indicating motivations, relevant academic and work experience, career plans and the chosen Major(s)/Minor(s) in order of preference.
7. Two recommendation letters from teachers/professors or job supervisors, explicitly assessing the student's ability to follow the EPOG-JM programme, each including date of issue, name, institution, position, signature, official stamp (if available) and contact details (phone and email).
8. Scanned copy of a valid passport (EU citizens only may use their ID card); applicants with multiple nationalities must use the passport of the nationality they apply with.
9. Only for Erasmus Mundus scholarship applicants: proof of place of residence issued no more than 12 months before the scholarship deadline (residence certificate, employer/institution confirmation letter, tax receipt, rental agreement or employment contract, flat owner's confirmation, or a utility invoice), plus the signed sworn statement on the applicant's place of residence over the past five years.
10. Optional: document detailing the applicant's own other funding (scholarships, funder name, value of award).
The UNITO microsite adds that the admission form downloadable from the EPOG website must be accompanied by a detailed curriculum, the certificate of previous exams, the cover letter, the research proposal for the Master's thesis and any other document useful to assess the acquired skills.
B. APPLY@UNITO (holders of a foreign qualification, postgraduate degrees): valid ID card (Italian/EU and equivalent) or valid passport (non-EU); residence permit valid for university enrolment for non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy (art. 39(5), Legislative Decree 286/1998); the first-cycle or integrated university degree obtained after at least 15 years of total schooling (EQF 6 / ISCED 6) with proof of authenticity, all pages included; the transcript of records listing all exams, marks, hours and/or credits, with proof of authenticity (a Diploma Supplement issued on the EU/Council of Europe/UNESCO model and containing the full transcript may replace both); curriculum vitae (mandatory); motivation letter in English or Italian (mandatory); syllabus (useful, not mandatory); Declaration of Value or CIMEA statement of comparability (not mandatory but may be requested); grading system explanation (may be requested). Documents are accepted in Italian, English, French or Spanish; otherwise a certified translation is required. Documents without signature, seal or stamp are not accepted and incomplete applications are not considered. Proof of authenticity: legalisation, Apostille, ENIC-NARIC statement of verification, or an official national digital verification platform.
C. FOR ENROLMENT - non-EU citizens residing abroad: valid passport, study visa, receipt of the residence-permit application, Italian fiscal code ('codice fiscale'), and study documents with proof of authenticity. EU/equivalents/non-EU legally residing in Italy: valid identification document, residence permit where applicable, Italian fiscal code, study documents with proof of authenticity. Enrolment itself is completed on MyUniTO (photo 35x40 mm, copy of a valid ID, copy of the social security number) and by paying the first instalment by the due date.

uncertainty_notes:
1) ACCESS PROBLEM. www.eap.unito.it and en.unito.it were unreachable by direct fetch during this research (connection refused / timeout on the unito.it origin, HTTP 403 from Apply@UniTo for the automated fetcher). Findings were assembled from: (a) apply.unito.it course 683 retrieved live with a browser user-agent via curl; (b) Wayback Machine snapshots of eap.unito.it 'Admission requirements' (snapshot 18 May 2025, page last updated 23/12/2024), 'Key information' (page last updated 05/01/2026), 'How to apply' (page last updated 31/03/2025) and 'Administrative procedures'; (c) Wayback snapshots of en.unito.it 'Postgraduate degrees with free admission', 'Application for international students' and 'Required documents for international students' carrying a.y. 2026-2027 content; (d) the live epog.eu consortium pages, which the UNITO microsite itself links to as the official application and fee pages. No unito.it page could be opened live, so all UNITO figures should be re-verified once the origin is reachable.
2) NOT A STAND-ALONE UNITO DEGREE. This is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EPOG-JM) with a joint title, awarded together with Université de technologie de Compiègne, Sorbonne Université, Conservatoire national des arts et métiers, and (for Path 2) the University of the Witwatersrand; the wider consortium also includes HWR Berlin, Roma Tre, Université de Genève, WU Wien, UFRJ and UNICAMP. Only Semester 1 (and Semester 2 in Path 1) is spent in Turin; Semester 4 is 'to be defined'. Physical mobility is compulsory for all enrolled students. Applicants should not treat this as a two-year-in-Turin programme.
3) APPLICATION IS NOT MADE ON APPLY@UNITO ALONE. The binding admission call is the EPOG consortium call (application.epog.eu). Apply@UniTo hosts the course record (id 683, intake 33) and, for foreign-qualification holders, the parallel UNITO application within 25 Nov 2025 - 29 Jan 2026, but the Apply@UniTo 'Apply now' button for a.y. 2026/27 is disabled and merely refers applicants to the EPOG form. It could not be verified whether an Apply@UniTo application is strictly mandatory in addition to the EPOG application for every category of applicant.
4) CREDIT-REQUIREMENT CONFLICT. UNITO 'Admission requirements' and Apply@UniTo state 18 CFU in economics + 6 in statistics; the UNITO 'How to apply' page and the EPOG site state 24 ECTS in economics + 6 in statistics or econometrics. EPOG explains the 18+6 figure as a lower threshold under which certain Majors/Minors 'can be considered' outstanding applicants, with conditional acceptance and remedial courses. The 24+6 figure should be treated as the operative standard.
5) ENGLISH-LEVEL CONFLICT. UNITO pages publish B2 / IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 87 / CAE B / CPE C; the live EPOG page publishes C1 / IELTS 7.0 / TOEFL iBT 95 / PTE 67 / CAE B / CPE C. Since the EPOG consortium runs the selection and its page is the more recently maintained one, applicants should plan for C1 / IELTS 7.0. The GRE alternative is also quoted on two different scales (150/4/151 on Apply@UniTo and EPOG; 450/4.1/650 on the UNITO microsite - old GRE scale).
6) FEE CONFLICT. Apply@UniTo still describes the EUR 1,000/year package as 600 tuition + 400 insurance for students with a personal income below EUR 15,000/year; the live EPOG page says EUR 1,000/year (of which about 500 is insurance) for students with a personal income below EUR 26,400/year, with EUR 9,600/year full fees above that threshold and a complete waiver for Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders. The EPOG page is the one linked as 'Partecipation costs' from the UNITO microsite and appears to be current; note also an internal inconsistency on that EPOG page itself, which mentions both 26,400 and 25,800 euros as the income threshold. Whether the ordinary UNITO regional tuition contribution (EUR 156-2,800/year by income) applies in addition could not be established - it appears NOT to, because the joint programme has its own consortium fee regime.
7) ADMISSION-TYPE AMBIGUITY. UNITO lists the programme among 'Postgraduate degrees with free admission' (no numerus clausus), yet Apply@UniTo publishes a 20-place quota for non-EU applicants residing abroad and the EPOG selection is genuinely competitive with a main list and a reserve list. No total number of places for EU applicants is published anywhere.
8) CYCLE COVERED. The a.y. 2026/2027 call (cohort 2026-2028) has already closed (deadline 29 January 2026). At the date of research (1 September 2026) the open/next cycle is cohort 2027-2029 (a.y. 2027/2028): platform opening October 2026, deadline 29 January 2027 at 13:00 Paris time. A second call for self-paying students (without an Erasmus Mundus scholarship) 'might be opened also later' according to EPOG's indicative timing, but no dates are published.
9) NON-UNITO SOURCE USE. The research brief asked for unito.it sources only. epog.eu was used because the UNITO microsite itself links to it as the official application ('How to apply' -> 'the online form on the EPOG web site') and fee ('Partecipation costs') destination, and because it is the only source carrying current 2027-2029 dates and the current language thresholds. Every epog.eu-derived statement is flagged as such above.
